title: Netanyahu Vows No Withdrawal from Gaza's Yellow Line After Israel Captures Hamas Internal Security Chief
detail: September 2, 2026 — Visiting an IDF outpost near Gaza's 'Yellow Line' alongside Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared 'We control the area, and we remain on this line' and that Israel is 'not withdrawing,' rejecting the core premise of the Board of Peace's phased withdrawal roadmap. On disarmament, Netanyahu said 'We are doing everything to reach our goal — the disarmament of Hamas and the demilitarization of Gaza,' claiming the objective has 'been achieved to a large extent' while acknowledging 'more work to complete,' and put Israeli control of the Strip at roughly 60%. The visit came a day after Shin Bet special forces, backed by IDF airstrikes, captured Muein al-Arabid — head of Hamas's internal security apparatus — in a raid in Gaza City, which Netanyahu called 'the first high-level capture operation deep in the Gaza Strip in a long time.' He said al-Arabid 'was responsible for hiding and moving our hostages, hiding senior Hamas officials, force build-up, and attempting to restore the capabilities of the terror organization,' and vowed Israel 'will continue to pursue all Hamas leaders' tied to October 7. The comments widen the gap between Israel's position and the Board of Peace's 15-point roadmap, which envisions a phased Israeli withdrawal tied to a transitional, UN-recognized administration.

title: Hamas Warns Gaza Ceasefire 'Could Collapse' After Israeli Raid Captures Its Internal Security Chief
detail: September 2, 2026 — Hamas's internal-security arm (Al-Majd al-Amni) warned that the already-shaky Gaza ceasefire could break down completely following the Sept. 1 Israeli special-forces raid that captured Moein Muhammad al-Arabeed, the group's internal-security chief, in Gaza City's Katiba area; the daylight operation was accompanied by strikes that Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry said killed 3-4 Palestinians. Hamas called the raid a deliberate attempt to 'undermine the ceasefire agreement, sabotage efforts to complete its implementation and create conditions for the continuation of the war.' Political analyst Emad Omar, cited by The National, said the operation 'could make the movement hesitant' to proceed with the disarmament provisions central to the ceasefire's second phase. Defense Minister Israel Katz defended the raid as Israeli 'policy: We do not wait for threats' — deepening the standoff described in Netanyahu's separate Yellow Line remarks the same day.
